name: Blaze SQL
description:
BlazeSQL lets Claude query your database or warehouse with all the necessary context to get the correct answers.

Connect to Snowflake, BigQuery, Redshift, Microsoft SQL Server, PostgreSQL, MySQL, AWS Athena, MariaDB, SQL Anywhere, Databricks, Clickhouse, and Oracle.

With context management, observability, and comprehensive access controls, BlazeSQL turns claude into an enterprise-ready AI Data Analyst for reliable self-service across your entire company.

As a comprehensive Business Intelligence layer, BlazeSQL also enables visualization, dashboards, advanced statistical analysis, predictive analytics, scheduled reports, and custom PDF or interactive HTML reports.

_published_faq.name: How do I add Blaze SQL to Claude, ChatGPT, or Cursor?

acceptedAnswer.text: Add Blaze SQL to Claude, ChatGPT, or Cursor by connecting its remote MCP URL in each client's MCP settings. In Claude, add a custom connector. In ChatGPT, add an MCP app. In Cursor, add an MCP server under Settings. The MCP URL is https://claude.blazesql.com/. This server requires OAuth, so complete the login prompt after you connect.

_published_faq.name: What tools does the Blaze SQL MCP server provide?

acceptedAnswer.text: Blaze SQL provides these MCP tools: describe_tables, execute_sql, graph_sql_result, list_dashboards, list_saved_queries, list_schemas, list_tables, read_dashboard, read_saved_query, search_dashboards, search_saved_queries, and suggest_schema_context_update.

_published_faq.name: What are the best alternatives to Blaze SQL?

acceptedAnswer.text: As of October 17, 2026, alternatives to Blaze SQL in data-analytics on the Manufact MCP catalog include Epicure, Newsflash, Point Topic, Pricing Optimizer AI, and StatCite.

_published_faq.name: Does Blaze SQL MCP require authentication?

acceptedAnswer.text: Blaze SQL requires authentication. Connect it in Claude, ChatGPT, or Cursor and complete the OAuth login prompt.
Blaze SQL is developed by BlazeSQL. It is listed as community on the Claude connector directory.
